I'd like to consider myself an 'old-school Conservative' in economic regard. Not a post-60s/80s "Free Market"-fundamentalist, but not a socialist either.

Decentralize the economy, prefer small/medium-sized businesses over multi-nationals (through preferential taxation, which is the opposite of what we have today)

Keep a safety-net for those in need, but organize local solutions so you don't have an underclass of subsidized couch-potatoes (apparently in the 1950s it wasn't uncommon in towns & villages to employ the handicapped while they only did small menial tasks. It was basically a welfare-on-the-local-employer scheme, that kept people secure from poverty while they still got to participate fully in their local community)

Certain services are best done publicly, police/firemen, public transport, road infrastructure, imo even schooling and healthcare benefit from being (partially) public. It is about trying to get the 'best of both worlds': Dutch schools would be a good example: publicly funded, but privately managed, with legal limits on how much donations they can solicit from parents. Similar healthcare schemes might work best for the people.

In a homogeneous high trust society we can keep people from living in poverty or permanent economic uncertainty (the modern day precariat economy of the self-employed) and I'd like to live in a country take care of each other rather than a Hobsian/Ayn Randian dystopia of 'eat or be eaten' / 'might makes right'.
